dish: roast pork with spinach and sharp provolone; cheesesteak
w: The South Philly shack (open since the 1930s) that Craig LaBan named the city's best cheesesteak in 2002 and that finished second in the Inquirer's 2023 bracket; its juicy roast pork with sautéed spinach earned a James Beard America's Classics award.

dish: roast pork with broccoli rabe and sharp provolone
address: Reading Terminal Market, 51 N 12th St, Philadelphia, PA 19107
w: Reading Terminal Market's roast-pork counter — #1 on Philadelphia Magazine's roast-pork list and The Infatuation's pick for the best sandwich in the market.

dish: roast pork on a Sarcone's roll
w: Italian Market sandwich counter serving roast pork on Sarcone's rolls with a choice of American, mild or sharp provolone, or Whiz — on both Visit Philly's and Philly Mag's roast-pork lists.

dish: tomato pie and seeded rolls
w: Century-old 9th Street bakery whose tomato pie, baked in a brick hearth oven, is crisp at the edges and juicy in the middle; its seeded rolls carry half the city's hoagies and roast pork.

dish: 'Depression-era' gravy tomato pie
w: Tomato pie pulled from a 115-year-old, 21-foot-deep brick oven, topped with a classic South Philly red gravy balanced with garlic, oregano and Pecorino Romano. Note: open only on a few announced days a year — check before going.

dish: lemon, cherry and pineapple water ice
w: On the corner of 7th and Christian since 1945, making water ice from nothing but water, sugar and fresh fruit.

dish: real-fruit water ice (white grape, coquito, mango-berry)
w: Started in 1995 by a Temple student; a West Philly favourite for water ice loaded with chunks of real fruit.

dish: 40 flavours from the marble counter
address: Reading Terminal Market, 51 N 12th St, Philadelphia, PA 19107
w: America's oldest ice-cream company (1861), run by the fifth and sixth generations of L.D. Bassett's family — it predates the market itself.

dish: fresh Pennsylvania Dutch doughnuts
address: Reading Terminal Market, 51 N 12th St, Philadelphia, PA 19107
w: Pennsylvania Dutch doughnuts since 1985 — around 40 varieties a day, stuffed, topped and drizzled, worth the line.

dish: blueberry pancakes, scrapple and apple dumplings
address: Reading Terminal Market, 51 N 12th St, Philadelphia, PA 19107
w: Amish-family Pennsylvania Dutch counter where you sit elbow-to-elbow; get the plate-sized blueberry pancakes.

dish: hand-rolled soft pretzels and pretzel dogs
address: Reading Terminal Market, 51 N 12th St, Philadelphia, PA 19107
w: Fluffier-than-usual soft pretzels with crisp, big-salted crusts that rip like cinnamon buns fresh from the oven.

dish: cheesesteak 'wit' or 'witout' onions
w: Where the cheesesteak began: hot-dog vendor Pat Olivieri started selling thin-sliced steak on a roll here in the 1930s (cheese came in the '40s). Measured honestly: it is the historic origin and a 24-hour 9th-and-Passyunk spectacle rather than critics' best steak — go for the history, go to Angelo's/Dalessandro's/John's for the sandwich.

dish: cheesesteak
w: Pat's neon-lit rival across the 9th-and-Passyunk intersection since 1966, also open 24/7 — part of the city's most famous food rivalry; kept as an icon, not as a critics' pick.

dish: cheesesteak with fried onions
w: Jim's (founded 1939 in West Philly) opened its Art Deco South Street shop on July 5, 1976 — the line on 4th and South is a South Street landmark.

dish: roast pork Italian, cheesesteak
w: The original East Oregon Avenue stand under the I-95 overpass, renamed Tony & Nick's Steaks in 2022 after a family legal settlement over the Tony Luke's name (Inquirer, 6abc); Craig LaBan's 2002 cheesesteak survey rated it among the city's best.

dish: sliced-to-order Italian hoagies; the Fig Pig
w: Craig LaBan used this Fishtown Italian market to explain what makes a great hoagie; Visit Philly lists its sliced-to-order hoagies including the Fig Pig (fig jam, prosciutto, mascarpone).

dish: Italian hoagie on a Sarcone's roll
w: A fifth-generation Italian deli in South Philly building hoagies of coteghino, mortadella, soppressata, capicola and prosciutto on Sarcone's rolls.

dish: Papale Special; Boujie Bucci tuna hoagie
w: Queen Village deli at the top of recent best-hoagie rankings, with a dozen cold hoagies on Cacia's rolls.

dish: hoagies and breakfast sandwiches
w: Matt Cahn's Washington Square West sandwich shop (with a Fishtown sibling) that rose fast into the city's best-hoagie ranks.

dish: the Daddy Wad; brisket Paesano
w: Chef Peter McAndrews' Italian Market sandwich shop of big, chef-driven hoagies like the Daddy Wad.

dish: beef pho
w: Philly's baseline pho — the benchmark the rest are judged against — in the Washington Avenue plaza; Anthony Bourdain ate breakfast pho here on The Layover.

dish: bánh mì on house-baked baguette
w: Little Saigon institution: bakery, market and bánh mì counter whose crisp-shelled, fluffy house baguette makes the sandwich.

dish: 12 kinds of pho; broad Vietnamese menu
w: The giant, old-school dining room in the Washington Avenue plaza with the area's most expansive Vietnamese menu — the lunch stop for Vietnamese tour groups visiting Philadelphia.

dish: Capulhuac-style lamb barbacoa tacos, pancita, consomé
w: Cristina Martinez's weekend barbacoa counter on South 9th Street; Martinez won the 2022 James Beard Best Chef: Mid-Atlantic. Weekends only, early, until the lamb runs out. Now operates from the Casa Mexico building at 1134 S 9th St (the two merged).

dish: tacos, enchiladas; the weekend barbacoa pushcart
w: Cristina Martinez's seven-day sister restaurant next door to South Philly Barbacoa; on weekends her yellow barbacoa pushcart works out front from 5am.

dish: rendang, greens, tofu from the buffet case
w: The Widjojo family's no-menu Indonesian steam-table in South Philly — Philadelphia has the second-largest Indonesian community in the US — a James Beard semifinalist (2018) famed for rendang and greens.

dish: seasonal New American; Sunday brunch
w: An 1850 roadhouse deep in the Wissahickon on Forbidden Drive, the only restaurant inside the park — hikers in trail gear welcome.
